posts.title: Mariners Beat Angels 7-3 as Los Angeles Ends Season With Franchise-Record 100 Losses
posts.description: Logan Gilbert struck out eight over four no-hit innings as the Seattle Mariners beat the Los Angeles Angels 7-3 in the regular-season finale for both teams. Five Seattle pitchers combined for 12 strikeouts as the Mariners finished the season at 76-86. The Angels closed at 62-100, reaching 100 losses for the first time in franchise history. Seattle also announced after the game that manager Dan Wilson will not return next season. Wilson finished his tenure with a 187-171 record after taking over for Scott Servais in August 2024. Gilbert Opens With Four No-Hit Innings Gilbert dominated the Angels during his abbreviated final start of the season. The right-hander retired the first 12 Los Angeles hitters he faced and struck out eight through four innings. Moisés Ballesteros drew a walk to begin the fifth, ending Gilbert’s run of 12 consecutive outs. Seattle then removed Gilbert, who received a standing ovation from the home crowd. posts.title: Taylor Ward, J.P. Crawford Power Mariners Past Angels 8-4
posts.description: Taylor Ward delivered a pinch-hit, two-run single in the seventh inning before J.P. Crawford followed with a two-run homer as the Seattle Mariners beat the Los Angeles Angels 8-4 on Saturday night. The Angels had erased a four-run deficit with a four-run sixth inning, but Seattle responded an inning later. Ward broke the 4-4 tie against Mitch Farris, and Crawford homered on the next pitch to give the Mariners a four-run advantage. Seattle also saw starter Kade Anderson leave in the fourth inning after Christian Moore hit a 104 mph line drive off his left arm. The Mariners later announced that Anderson sustained a left forearm bruise. Anderson Leaves After Strong Start Anderson controlled the Angels through the first three innings. The Seattle left-hander completed 3 1/3 scoreless innings before his night ended abruptly. Moore hit a 104 mph line drive that struck Anderson on the left arm in the fourth. posts.title: Reid Detmers Throws Six Shutout Innings as Angels Hold Off Mariners 7-5
posts.description: Reid Detmers pitched six scoreless innings, and Wade Meckler collected four hits as the Los Angeles Angels held off a late Seattle Mariners rally for a 7-5 win on Friday night. Detmers allowed only two hits while striking out seven, and Meckler finished a home run short of the cycle. Christian Moore hit a three-run homer, while Zach Neto added his team-leading 27th homer and an RBI double. The Angels carried a 6-0 lead into the eighth before Seattle scored five times over the final two innings. Los Angeles survived the late push after Randy Arozarena tripled and Dominic Canzone hit a two-run homer in the ninth. Detmers Controls Seattle Detmers kept the Mariners without a hit through the first three innings. The left-hander retired the Seattle lineup without allowing a hit until Canzone singled with one out in the fourth. That did not lead to a run.
